text: Fellow agents — which lenders do you actually trust to close on time? I've had two escrows blow past their close date this month because the loan didn't clear underwriting in time and I'm losing patience. Drop who you use (and who to avoid) below.
comment_source_reason: Real-estate agents publicly asking which lenders close on time draws direct pitches from loan officers (competitors for the MLO) and recommendations from other agents (partner-segment leads for the MLO); since almost every commenter is an agent, the same thread is mostly noise for a realtor client except where the agent is actually serving Orange County, in which case they are a competitor rather than a lead.

comments: I close in 18 days average, happy to be your backup lender — message me and I'll show you my pipeline.
Honestly it's less the lender and more the loan officer. I use Sarah at Pacific Home Loans, she's never missed a close date.
My go-to is a broker at CrossCountry, closes in 21 days flat every time, worth it even if the rate is slightly higher.
I switched to a local credit union lender last year and haven't had a late close since.
Rates aside, the real issue is agents not sending complete files. Send me your buyer's docs and I'll show you a real 20-day close.
We deal with this in Sacramento too honestly, our go-to lender closes in 21 days like clockwork.

comments: Same story down in San Diego, half the lenders don't communicate until day 25.
From the escrow side, it's almost always a stalled condition on the loan, not us — happy to walk anyone through it.

Also — I'm actually about to list my own place in Tustin, so extra motivated to find a lender that won't blow my buyer's close date lol.

rows.author_line: Real Estate Photographer, OC Listing Media
comments: As a listing photographer I hear this complaint from agents constantly, it's brutal for marketing timelines.
My best advice: ask for the LO's actual pull-through rate, not just the company's marketing close time.
We had one close in 11 days last month, still can't believe it, definitely sharing that LO's info.
Title's rarely the bottleneck honestly, it's almost always loan conditions clearing late.

Adding my two cents — ask the LO how many files they're juggling, overloaded LOs are the real problem.
My buyers keep getting stuck at the appraisal-to-clear-to-close gap, not sure that's even fixable.
